title: Lithium‐Ion Battery Storage: A Cross‐Scale Review From the Energy Storage Ecosystem to Application‐Specific Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Energy storage underpins the decarbonization of power systems, and lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) have become the dominant platform for modular, fast‐response deployment in both stationary and mobile applications. However, LIB research is frequently examined in isolation from the wider storage landscape, leaving its technological positioning, applicability boundaries, and systemic role insufficiently clarified. This study establishes the linkage from field‐wide storage functions through application‐specific duty cycles to degradation pathways and battery management priorities, thereby translating bibliometric structures into deployment‐oriented guidance. Two logically nested corpora were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for 2021–2025, comprising 30 141 records for the field‐wide layer and 8902 for the focused layer, and document co‐citation networks were constructed in CiteSpace. The field‐wide map resolves into a three‐dimensional structure spanning technical characteristics, operational optimization and intelligent management, and application scenarios and business models. The focused map differentiates into stationary storage and electric vehicle branches, compared in duty cycles, degradation drivers, battery management priorities, and end‐of‐life roles. The synthesis explicitly maps stationary duty cycles to corresponding degradation pathways and emphasizes path‐dependent prognostics under dynamic operating sequences, addressing the gap between laboratory testing and field deployment. The review synthesizes progress in advanced battery management, system integration, and circular life cycle strategies, with each technical direction mapped to its underlying economic mechanism across four analytical layers. Three research priorities are identified: evidence from real operation across the full life cycle, state perception coupling multiple physical domains, and intelligent coordination of diverse storage technologies.
title_zh: Lithium‐Ion Battery Storage: A Cross‐Scale Review From the Energy Storage Ecosystem to Application‐Specific Management

title: Interpretable and uncertainty-quantified early remaining useful life prediction for lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols
abstract: Under fast-charging protocols, accurately and interpretably predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries during the initial cycling stage is of great significance for early fault warning and reliability assessment. To improve the interpretability of RUL prediction, this paper proposes a causal learning approach to conduct causal analysis on domain-specific features, identifying key causal variables and systematically uncovering their relationships with RUL. To enhance the model’s capacity to fit complex nonlinear relationships and generalize across various conditions, we propose a neural network based on Legendre polynomial orthogonal bases, termed LegendreNet. Its approximation ability and theoretical validity are rigorously demonstrated. The causally selected domain features are fed into LegendreNet for prediction. In parallel, the original features are fed into a causal convolutional neural network (CCNN) to extract deep representations, capturing both global spatiotemporal dependencies and local feature details. The outputs of LegendreNet and CCNN are then concatenated and fused via LegendreNet to generate the final RUL prediction. Based on this architecture, we propose a novel multimodal prediction framework for early RUL estimation of lithium-ion batteries, named LNCCNN. Finally, to adaptively adjust the bandwidth and quantify predictive uncertainty, we introduce curvature adjustment into the Bayesian bootstrap kernel density estimation (BB-KDE) framework and propose a novel method, called curvature-aware BB-KDE (CA-BB-KDE). Experimental results on two distinct batches from the same fast-charging dataset demonstrate improved early RUL prediction accuracy, reducing RMSE by 2.96% and 7.09% and MAPE by 1.32% and 8.16%, respectively, supporting lifetime monitoring and decision-making in battery management systems.
title_zh: Interpretable and uncertainty-quantified early remaining useful life prediction for lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols

title: HIC-LLM: Health-Indicator Consistency Scoring and Optional Evidence-Grounded Large Language Model Reporting
abstract: Pack-level state-of-health assessment can conceal the cell that first reaches its lower-voltage limit and constrains a series-connected backup battery string. Cell-level localization is therefore required, but the scarcity of labeled field events and high-resolution telemetry does not support training or validating a supervised, unsupervised, or semi-supervised model. General-purpose language models introduce a separate risk of unsupported causal interpretation. These limitations motivate a two-stage framework: a training-free health-indicator consistency (HIC) score performs all numerical localization through within-event, one-sided median-absolute-deviation normalization, and an optional language model converts only the fixed ranking and structured evidence into an author-audited maintenance report with bounded mechanisms and explicit uncertainty. The primary evidence comprises two capacity-test reports from the same 24-cell, 2-V, 100-Ah pack: a manually terminated reference test and one lower-voltage-limit event. A separate CR-BTM workbook contributes 46 low-current pack-level records and 1104 cell-monitor records, but lacks a unique pack or device identifier, calendar date, capacity integration, and termination reason; it is therefore treated only as a candidate ancillary dataset with compatible measurement characteristics. In the lower-voltage-limit event, Cell #6 reached 1.800 V, released capacity was 86.11 Ah versus 100.46 Ah in the reference event, and HIC ranked Cell #6 first with a score of 7.983, compared with 1.145 for the runner-up. Cell #6 also had the largest lower-tail score at every recorded pre-termination time, including the record approximately 0.57 h before termination. Direct final-voltage and voltage-drop rules also rank Cell #6 first; consequently, the result is an engineering consistency verification of one field-confirmed event, not evidence of predictive superiority or population-level performance.
title_zh: HIC-LLM: Health-Indicator Consistency Scoring and Optional Evidence-Grounded Large Language Model Reporting

title: A physics-informed framework with proximal policy optimization for lithium-ion battery state-of-health estimation
abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation across laboratory protocols and field operation requires a model that can follow changing degradation behavior without imposing one physics weighting over an entire service life. This study develops a physics-informed estimator whose constraint schedule is controlled by proximal policy optimization (PPO). Parallel multiscale causal convolutions feed a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder and temporal attention. The objective combines three always-active prediction constraints with three dimensionless latent-field modules for polarization–resistance–thermal balance, solid- and electrolyte-phase transport, and solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth. At scheduled decision points, the controller admits eligible modules and redistributes a nonnegative fixed-sum weight budget from multiscale residual evidence. Across five prespecified random seeds, the proposed method achieves seed-averaged root-mean-square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.656% SOH, 0.479% SOH, and 0.510% on the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) dataset; 1.212% SOH, 0.834% SOH, and 0.901% on the Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU) dataset; and 1.277%, 0.992%, and 1.147% for the electric-vehicle (EV) capacity index. The corresponding sample standard deviations are reported in Section 4.3 . Projected schedules preserve the fixed weight sum to numerical precision and require no deadline override.
title_zh: A physics-informed framework with proximal policy optimization for lithium-ion battery state-of-health estimation

title: Two-stage model predictive control for battery electric vehicle-centric mobile energy storage in microgrids
abstract: With the accelerated global energy transition, integrating battery electric vehicles into microgrid systems has emerged as a promising approach to enhance operational flexibility and reduce energy storage infrastructure costs. This paper proposes a two-stage model predictive control framework for real-time energy dispatch in grid-connected microgrids, in which battery electric vehicles are treated as the dominant mobile energy storage resources, while stationary battery energy storage systems serve only an auxiliary role. A dynamic electricity-pricing mechanism guides vehicle charging and discharging behavior and couples the two control stages. In the first stage, feasible charging and discharging power ranges are determined based on user preference modeling, explicitly considering state of charge, travel demand, and price responsiveness. In the second stage, a quadratic programming problem is solved to obtain the cost-minimizing dispatch strategy while satisfying power balance and operational constraints. Tidal energy is integrated with wind and PV to form a more predictable renewable portfolio. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the vehicle-dominated architecture yields an extra daily economic benefit of 494.15 ¥ over the conventional stationary storage-dominated scheme, representing an approximately 225% increase in system savings. The framework also maintains stable performance under high-load scenarios while fully satisfying travel requirements. These results provide theoretical insights into microgrid energy management and the deployment of vehicle-to-grid technologies.
title_zh: Two-stage model predictive control for battery electric vehicle-centric mobile energy storage in microgrids
